name: Sagittarius A*
characteristics: Supermassive black hole at the Galactic Centre, imaged by the Event Horizon Telescope in 2022. Seen through dense dust in visible light, so it is observed mainly in radio, infrared and X-rays.
discovery: Balick & Brown, 1974 (radio source); mass from stellar orbits (Genzel, Ghez)
source: SIMBAD (CDS) and Gaia DR3 astrometry, compiled from published values

name: M87*
characteristics: Supermassive black hole at the centre of M87. First black hole ever imaged directly (EHT, 2019). Drives a relativistic jet roughly 5,000 light-years long.
discovery: Imaged by the Event Horizon Telescope, 2019
source: NASA/IPAC Extragalactic Database (NED), compiled from published values

name: TON 618
classification: Hyperluminous quasar (powered by a black hole)
distance_note: Light-travel distance derived from redshift z = 2.219 (ΛCDM, approximate)
characteristics: Extremely luminous quasar powered by one of the most massive black holes known. Published mass estimates are of order 10^10 solar masses and differ between methods, so no single value is given here.
discovery: Radio source catalogued in the Tonantzintla catalogue; identified as a quasar in 1970s
source: NASA/IPAC Extragalactic Database (NED), compiled from published values

name: Cygnus X-1
characteristics: First strong black-hole candidate, discovered as an X-ray source. The black hole accretes material stripped from its supergiant companion.
discovery: X-ray source detected by rocket flight, 1964; identified as a black-hole candidate in the 1970s
source: SIMBAD (CDS) and Gaia DR3 astrometry, compiled from published values
